Occupying an extensive area of more than 20 mow 
of land and towering above the ground four stories in 
height, the heavy-built, concrete-steel-reinforced new 
Japanese barracks at the end of North Szechuen Road, 
Officially known as the Headquarters of the Japanese 
Naval Landing Party in Shanghai, was thrown open for 
inspection by a group of Chinese and foreign newspaper- 
men last Friday, Sept. 15. The barracks is located at a 
strategic point in the Settlement Extension. It com- 
mands an extensive view over the newly developed 
Chineze Municipal Center in Kiangwan and is right on 
the edge of Chapei, the scene of last year’s hostilities. 
Costing more than Yer 1,500,000 and providing accom- 
modation gor over 3,000 men, this enormous structure 
was started in Dec. 1932 and is now in its final stages 
of completion. ‘Right adjacent to it, is the newly-built 
Japanese military hospital. Viewed in every aspect, the 
new Japanese barracks presents an appearance of a 
permanent military establighment and can easily be con- 
verted into a stronghold in case of war. The building 
stands as a striking contrast to the temporary quarters 
of the troops of other foreign powers in Shanghai which 
are either cheap wooden shacks or rented houses. The 
construction of such a permanent military establishment 
in Shanghai is a direct violation of the Nine Power 
Treaty signed at Washington in 1922 on the part of 
Japan, which stipulates for the gradual withdrawal o7 
all foreign troops in Shanghai. According to inquiries

ing was constructed with neither notice to nor permission 
from the Chinese authorities in whose territory it is 
situated or the Shanghai Municipal Council. Even, the 
Consular representatives of the Powers in Shanghai were 
not notified. The ,entire business was done in utmost 
secrecy and it did not attract much attention, until the 
building has recently been completed.

Subject (in full) Extension of buildings of the Japanese Naval Barracks on
Kiangwan Road.

Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by （签名）

An extension building to the barracks of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party is under construction on Kiangwan Road to
the north of the former barracks. The new building is being
constructed of steel, cement and brick and will have a dimension
of about 120 feet by 40 feet. One-third of the building will
be of three storeys, another third of two storeys and the
remaining third of one storey. The building will be used as work-

September 23, 1933 THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. No. D Date ____）

Japanese Barracks Thrown Open for
Laymen Inspection

Occupying an extensive area of more than 20 mow
of land and towering above the ground four stories in
height, the heavy-built, concrete-steel-reinforced new
Japanese barracks at the end of North Szechuen Road,
officially known as the Headquarters of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party in Shanghai, was thrown open for
inspection by a group of Chinese and foreign newspaper-
men last Friday, Sept. 15. The barracks is located at a
strategic point in the Settlement Extension. It com-
mands an extensive view over the newly developed
Chinese Municipal Center in Kiangwan and is right on
the edge of Chapei, the scene of last year's hostilities.
Costing more than Yen 1,500,000 and providing accom-
modation for over 3,000 men, this enormous structure
was started in Dec. 1932 and is now in its final stages
of completion. Right adjacent to it, is the newly-built
Japanese military hospital. Viewed in every aspect, the
new Japanese barracks presents an appearance of a
permanent military establishment and can easily be con-
verted into a stronghold in case of war. The building
stands as a striking contrast to the temporary quarters
of the troops of other foreign powers in Shanghai which
are either cheap wooden shacks or rented houses. The
construction of such a permanent military establishment
in Shanghai is a direct violation of the Nine Power
Treaty signed at Washington in 1922 on the part of
Japan, which stipulates for the gradual withdrawal of
all foreign troops in Shanghai. According to inquiries
made at the new Japanese Naval Headquarters, the build-
ing was constructed with neither notice to nor permission
from the Chinese authorities in whose territory it is
situated or the Shanghai Municipal Council. Even, the
Consular representatives of the Powers in Shanghai were
not notified. The entire business was done in utmost
secrecy and it did not attract much attention, until the
building has recently been completed.

Escorted by Commander K. Kakuta, Senior Staff Officer
of the Barracks, and several English-speaking Japanese
guides, a party of more than 50 press representatives and
photographers was conducted to inspect the building from
the roof to the basement. The roof is a flat open space with
an observation tower, two large water tanks and three or
four concrete-built washing tubs. The Observation
tower consists of two stories, the upper story being built
of steel plates about two inches in thickness. While the
newspaper visitors were pacing the roof, Commander
Kakuta remarked that the roof was very weak and could
not sustain gun emplacements. But the newspaper men
were all of the opinion that the roof was certainly strongly
built. But whether it could hold larger guns, it is rather a
matter for experts to decide, while the laymen news
reporters could only guess and accept what they were told
by the Japanese guides. The roof has considerable open
space and appears to be sufficiently wide for an airplane to
land and hop off. On the roof were noticed two Hotchkiss
double barrelled anti-aircraft guns which were housed in
a little room not far from the observation tower.

Looking down from the roof into the compound, troop
units of various descriptions were marching in and out of
the enclosed court-yard every few moments, while others
stood in formation, executed brief drills, went about tasks
known only to themselves and their officers. It appeared
that the Headquarters were just receiving a consignment
of armament from Japan and men were busy with unload-
ing the "goods" cased in oblong wooden boxes which
Chinese reporters mistook for coffins. Bustling
activity was the note predominant at the barracks. Every-
thing looked serious and every man was on his job
of some kind. As a finishing touch to the building's con-
struction in the roof, a party of Chinese workmen was seen
completing a shrine and a stone tablet erected to the
memory of the Japanese soldiers and sailors who lost
their lives during the Shanghai hostilities in 1932.

From the roof, the party of newspaper men was con-
ducted through the various stories of the building.

There was an almost endless series of sailors' quarters,
officers' rooms, recreation halls, gymnasiums; more quar-
ters for sailors who sleep mostly on swinging canvases.
Immediately adjoining each large room serving as men's
quarters, were smaller storerooms for rifles and numerous
sub-machine guns. On the second floor at a corner, was
noticed a number of paper tablets and inquiries disclosed
the fact that they were tablets of the sailors who died
in Shanghai of the recent epidemic of dysentery. They
were shortly to be sent back to Japan to their respective
homes.

The ground floor is largely devoted to garages for
armored cars, field guns, trench mortars, tanks and
repair shops. Of the larger guns now stored at the
barracks, officers stated that there were 30 three and six
inch guns, 18 armored tanks, four armored cars and some
2,000 men and officers on the premises.

Official dedication of the barracks will be held some
time in October when Japanese naval maneuvers will be
held before Admiral Yamamoto of the Naval Department
at Tokyo. The Commander of the Shanghai Japanese
Naval Landing Party is Rear-Admiral T. Sugimoto. He
is a graduate of the Japanese Naval Academy and was
Commander of a Japanese battleship prior to his Shanghai
Command.

（批：File 245. SEP. 25 1933）

日本兵营向非专业人士开放参观

占地超过 20 亩，高达四层，这座厚重的钢筋混凝土结构的新日本兵营位于北四川路尽头，官方名称为“上海日本海军陆战队司令部”，于上周五（9 月 15 日）向一群中外新闻记者开放参观。该兵营位于租界扩展区的战略要地。它可以俯瞰江湾新开发的中国市中心广阔区域，且紧邻去年战事发生地闸北的边缘。这座耗资超过 150 万日元、可容纳 3000 多人的庞大建筑于 1932 年 12 月动工，目前已进入最后完工阶段。紧邻其旁的是新建的日本军用医院。从各方面来看，这座新的日本兵营呈现出永久性军事设施的面貌，在战争情况下很容易转化为堡垒。该建筑与在上海的其他外国军队临时驻地形成鲜明对比，后者要么是廉价的木屋，要么是租赁的房屋。在上海建造如此永久性的军事设施，直接违反了日本于 1922 年在华盛顿签署的《九国公约》，该条约规定所有驻沪外国军队应逐步撤出。据向新的日本海军司令部查询得知，该建筑在建设时既未通知也未获得其所在领土的中国当局或上海公共租界工部局的许可。甚至在上海的各强国领事代表也未获通知。整个事宜在极度保密中进行，直到最近建筑完工才引起较多关注。

在兵营高级参谋官 K. Kakuta 指挥官及几位懂英语的日本向导的陪同下，一行 50 多名记者代表和摄影师对建筑从屋顶到地下室进行了参观。屋顶是一个平坦的开阔空间，设有一座瞭望塔、两个大型水箱和三四个混凝土建造的洗涤槽。瞭望塔分为两层，上层由约两英寸厚的钢板建成。当报纸访客在屋顶踱步时，Kakuta 指挥官称屋顶非常薄弱，无法承受火炮阵地。但记者们均认为屋顶确实建造得很坚固。至于能否承载更大口径的火炮，这更多是专家决定的事情，而非专业的新闻记者只能猜测并接受日本向导告知的内容。屋顶有相当大的开阔空间，看起来足够宽，可供飞机降落和起飞。在屋顶上，人们注意到两挺霍奇基斯双管高射炮，它们被安置在离瞭望塔不远的一个小房间里。

从屋顶向下俯瞰院落，各种部队单位每隔几分钟就在封闭的庭院中进进出出，而其他士兵则列队站立，进行简短的操练，忙于只有他们自己和军官知道的任务。看来司令部刚刚收到一批从日本运来的军火，士兵们正忙着卸下装在长方形木箱里的“货物”，中国记者误以为这些木箱是棺材。繁忙的活动是兵营的主要基调。一切看起来都很严肃，每个人都在从事某种工作。作为屋顶建筑施工的收尾工作，可以看到一群中国工人正在完成一座神社和一块石碑的建设，以纪念在 1932 年上海战事中丧生的日本士兵和水手。

记者从屋顶被引导穿过建筑的各个楼层。

那里有一连串几乎无尽的水兵宿舍、军官房间、娱乐厅、健身房；还有更多供水兵居住的宿舍，他们大多睡在吊床上。在每个作为士兵宿舍的大房间旁边，都有较小的储藏室，存放步枪和大量冲锋枪。在二楼的一个角落，注意到一些纸质牌位，经询问得知，这些是近期因痢疾流行而在上海去世的水兵的牌位。它们不久将被送回日本各自的家乡。

底层主要用于停放装甲车、野战炮、战壕迫击炮、坦克的车库以及修理车间。关于目前储存在兵营的大型火炮，军官称有 30 门三英寸和六英寸火炮，18 辆装甲坦克，四辆装甲车，以及现场约有 2000 名士兵和军官。

兵营的正式落成典礼将于 10 月的某个时候举行，届时东京海军部的山本上将将在场观看日本海军演习。上海日本海军陆战队司令是杉本 T. 少将。他是日本海军学院的毕业生，在担任上海司令之前曾是一艘日本战列舰的舰长。

（批：存档 245. 1933 年 9 月 25 日）

September 20, 33.
Report on arrival of Vice-Admiral Nomura by flagship
the "Izumo".

No. 1

With reference to the reports on the subject of
arrival of the New Commander-in-Chief Vice Admiral Nomura
of the Third Fleet of the Japanese Navy by the Flagship
"Izumo". I have to report that the "Izumo" came in from
yesterday will arrive at 3 p.m. September 20, and will
tie up at the British Naval Depot opposite the Club.
The following is the program arranged by
Japanese Consulate:

3.30 p.m. September 20; Vice-Admiral Nomura,
Japanese Naval attaché and staff officers will leave the
Customs Jetty for the Flagship.

3.50 p.m. September 20; The Japanese military
attaché, staff officers and Consul General Ishii and
leading local Japanese residents will leave the Customs
Jetty for the Flagship.

Both parties will leave the Jetty by naval
launch and are expected to return at about 6 p.m.
It is learned that Admiral Nomura will not leave the
ship today.

The programme of his movements on September 21
are as far as can be ascertained as follows:-

At 8.05 a.m. the Vice-Admiral will leave the
Flagship and inspect Japanese warships lying in the river.

At 9 a.m. he will make an official visit to Japanese
Minister in China and Japanese Consul-General at the Japanese
Consulate, 1 Yangtze Road.

The point of his landing is unknown at present.

From 1.30 p.m. he will receive greetings from
local Japanese residents at the Japanese Club on Bund Road.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 16, 1933
7233

Japanese Barracks Are Not
Fortress, As Rumoured

Journalists Inspect New Kiangwan Road Structure
Yesterday And Find No Gun Emplacements, Only
Building Adequate For Housing Of Troops

The newly constructed Japanese barracks on North Szechuen and Kiangwan Roads, which have been the subject of much recent antagonistic criticism in the vernacular press, were thrown open to the prying eyes of journalists yesterday afternoon.

Much has been made of the secrecy which cloaked the erection of the barracks, and the Chinese press has published several articles comparing the barracks to a fortress and explaining the potentialities.

Of secrecy yesterday there was little, the invitation of the Japanese authorities included qualified representatives of any newspaper or journal, and the group which inspected the barracks included reporters from three outstanding Chinese newspapers as well as from the Japanese, Russian, and foreign dailies of Shanghai.

Not A Fort

The first thing to be said about the barracks is that the building does not in any way resemble a fort, but seem to be exactly what it is named: a large, modern, well-constructed structure equipped for the housing of some 2,000 troops and their equipment.

While the appearance of the barracks is massive, it is not any more so than that of any four storey structure built for permanence and strength. Indeed, the building resembles, more than anything else, a modern factory.

Imagine a large rectangular box with the top off, a long side facing on Kiangwan Road and a short end resting on North Szechuen Road . . . that is the general appearance of the building. The dimensions are: 120 metres along Kiangwan Road and 65 metres on North Szechuen Road. The total cost is placed at 1,500,000 Yen.

Concrete Only Facing

The building is composed of three storeys placed above a high ground floor, the whole enclosing a large compound. Although the foundations and ground floor are of concrete, the three upper floors are made of tile faced with concrete, according to the Japanese authorities. This would seem to do away with the rumour that the structure was so erected that it could withstand heavy gun fire.

The interior of the building is well-lighted from rows of large windows. It has been asserted that these windows were made of such a design that they could be turned into machine gun emplacements. From observation it would seem that such is no more the case than for any ordinary window, and, indeed, would probably be inferior for such use to the ordinary window, because of the extra height.

There are no gun emplacements on the roof, and the only thing pertaining to guns which was to be seen above the ground floor were the carriages for two anti-aircraft guns which were housed on the roof.

Ground Floor Garages

The ground floor contains garages for automobiles, some 30 field pieces, and 13 armoured cars and tanks; rooms for the storage of supplies, a boiler room, and kitchens.

The three upper floors have the living quarters of the men and officers (the ranks sleep in hammocks), dining rooms, bath rooms, and other necessary places. There is no arsenal unless ordinary repair shops could be so considered.

Everything about the place was in clean shape despite the fact that construction of certain parts is still under way and that portions of the interior are not yet finished.

The roof is equipped with apparatus for the washing and drying of clothes and contains, with the exception of the anti-aircraft gun carriages already mentioned, no signs of artillery or machine gun mountings.

Shinto Shrine

At the corner of North Szechuen and Kiangwan Roads there is a watch tower from which a wonderful view can be seen in every direction. Beneath the tower is the Shinto Shrine which commemorates the deaths occurring last year. It is to be dedicated next month. The date for the official opening of the shrine has not yet been set, but will probably take place next month after completion with a visit by General Park.

日军兵营并非如谣传般的堡垒

记者昨日视察江湾路新建筑，未发现炮位，仅见足以容纳驻军的建筑

位于北四川路与江湾路的新建日本兵营，近期在华文报刊中遭受诸多敌意批评，昨日下午向好奇的记者们开放参观。

此前，兵营建造过程笼罩在神秘之中，此事被大肆渲染，华文报刊发表数篇文章，将兵营比作堡垒并剖析其潜在能力。

昨日却鲜有神秘可言，日本当局的邀请对象包括任何报纸或期刊的合格代表，视察兵营的团体中既有来自三家著名中文报纸的记者，也有来自上海日文、俄文及外文日报的记者。

并非堡垒

关于该兵营，首先要说的是，这座建筑丝毫不像堡垒，而恰恰如其名所示：是一座大型、现代、结构良好的建筑，配备设施以容纳约2000名士兵及其装备。

虽然兵营外观庞大，但并不比任何为持久和坚固而建造的四层建筑更甚。事实上，该建筑更像一座现代工厂。

想象一个去掉顶部的大型长方体盒子，长边面向江湾路，短端位于北四川路……这就是该建筑的大致外观。尺寸为：沿江湾路120米，沿北四川路65米。总造价估计为150万日元。

仅表面为混凝土

该建筑由高出地面的底层及其上的三层组成，整体围合出一个大院子。据日本当局称，虽然地基和底层为混凝土结构，但上面三层为瓷砖贴面并覆以混凝土。这似乎消除了该建筑结构旨在抵御重型炮火的谣言。

建筑内部通过成排的大窗户获得良好采光。有人声称这些窗户的设计使其能转变为机枪射击孔。但从观察来看，情况并非如此，与普通窗户无异；事实上，由于高度额外增加，用于此目的可能还不如普通窗户。

屋顶上没有炮位，除地面以上可见的两门高射炮的炮架（存放于屋顶）外，没有其他与火炮相关的设施。

底层车库

底层设有汽车车库、约30门野战炮、13辆装甲车和坦克；物资储藏室、锅炉房和厨房。

上面三层设有士兵和军官的生活区（士兵睡在吊床上）、餐厅、浴室和其他必要场所。除非将普通修理车间视为军火库，否则此处没有军火库。

尽管部分区域的施工仍在进行，且内部部分尚未完工，但该处的一切均保持整洁。

屋顶配备了洗衣和烘干衣物的设备，除前述的高射炮炮架外，没有任何火炮或机枪底座的迹象。

神道教神社

在北四川路与江湾路的拐角处有一座瞭望塔，从那里可以向各个方向看到极好的视野。塔下是纪念去年死亡人员的神道教神社。该神社将于下月落成。神社正式开放的日期尚未确定，但可能会在下月完工后，由白川将军（General Park，音译）访问期间举行。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 16, 1933
440

Japanese Barracks At
Hongkew Park Thrown
Open For Inspection

Shanghai Pressmen Tour New Structure That
Houses Naval Landing Party, Noting Plans
For Defense, Strength, Gun Emplacements;
Troops Busy As Ants In Huge Shanghai Home

Japanese sailors,—many of them
scarcely out of their teens and as
curious of their visitors as were the
visitors of the new Hongkew Park
barracks—were to be seen in every
phase of military life in their new
and modern four-story brick-and-
concrete "home" out at the end of
North Szechuen Road early yester-
day afternoon.

The barracks building, officially
known as the headquarters for the
Japanese Naval Landing Party in
Shanghai, was thrown open to the
inspection of local newspapermen
yesterday.

From Top To Bottom

Escorted to the roof, a party of
nearly 50 Shanghai newspaper re-
porters, photographers and foreign
news service correspondents began
the long journey of inspecting the
barracks building under the direc-
tion of English-speaking Japanese
guides.

Directly adjoining the elevated
observation tower on the rounded
front corner of the roof (which in
reality gives the sentry constantly
on observation duty the increased
height of two additional stories) is
a small Shinto shrine where sailors
in the barracks building can
worship without leaving the prem-
ises.

Looking down from the roof into
the compound troop units of vari-
ous descriptions were marching in
and out of the enclosed yard every
few moments while others stood in
formation awaiting further drill and
commands.

A question upon which no two
reporters present agreed was the
strength of the concrete roof of
the 525 by 225-foot building.
Those holding the opinion the
roof was of no more than ordi-
nary construction were violently
opposed by those who pointed to
concrete tanks placed in the cen-
ter of the roof for laundering pur-
pose, saying a contractor would
not risk placing such tanks on a
roof unless it were amply rein-
forced.

Guns Aplenty

Appeal to one of the Japanese
guides brought the statement that
heavy artillery would not be fired
from the top of the structure. The
discussion ended.

Walking to the rear, the group
of journalists and literary ob-
servers was greeted with the sight
of two double mounted anti-air-
craft guns, housed in small re-
doubts. When one of the petty
officers stationed on the roof was
asked by a China Press represen-
tative, through the Japanese
guide-interpreter, as to the num-
ber of such anti-aircraft weapons
at the barracks, his cryptic
answer was, "Plenty."

Going to the third and second
floors of the barracks the party
was taken through seemingly end-
less sailor's quarters, past officers'
rooms and into recreation halls,
bathrooms and mess quarters for
sailors. Immediately adjoining
each large room serving as quar-
ters for the troops were smaller
storerooms for rifles and ammuni-
tion and machine guns.

Armored Cars Housed
Of the larger pieces housed in
the barracks officials stated that
the total is 30 pieces and includes
artillery pieces from three to
eight inches in size. They are
said to include trench mortars
and small field pieces.

There are a total of nine armor-
ed cars and four tanks housed in
the storage space of the structure,
although the room occupied by
the guns, cars and tanks occupies
but a small portion of available
under-cover storage space for
such implements of war.

Storage rooms for munitions
and radio broadcasting equipment
were not opened to the inspection
of press visitors. No attempt was
made on the part of the Japanese
guides or military to prevent the
taking of pictures of the building
or compound.

Official dedication of the bar-
racks will not be held until some
(Continued on Page 18, Col. 3.)

(Continued from Page 13, Col. 2.)
time in October when Japanese
naval maneuvers will be held be-
fore Admiral Yarnamoto, of the
Navy Department at Tokyo.

The commander of the Shang-
hai Japanese Naval Landing Party
is Rear-admiral T. Sugisaka. Ad-
miral Sugisaka is a graduate of
the Japan Naval Academy and
was commander of a Japanese
battleship prior to his Shanghai
commission.

《大美晚报》（The China Press），1933年9月16日，星期六
440

虹口公园日军兵营
开放供视察

上海报界人士参观容纳海军登陆部队的新建筑，关注防御计划、强度、炮位； troops 在这座巨大的上海寓所中忙碌如蚁

日本水兵——其中许多人刚过青少年时期，他们对访客的好奇心不亚于访客对新的虹口公园兵营的好奇心——昨天下午早些时候，在北四川路尽头的这座新建四层砖混结构“家园”中，随处可见他们军事生活的各个方面。

这座兵营建筑，官方称为上海日本海军登陆部队总部，昨日向当地新闻记者开放视察。

从上到下

在近50名上海报纸记者、摄影师和外国通讯社通讯员的带领下，在一位讲英语的日本向导的指导下，开始了对兵营建筑的漫长视察之旅。

紧邻屋顶圆角前端的高架瞭望塔（实际上使常在此执行观察任务的哨兵增加了两层楼的高度）旁边，有一座小型神道教神社，兵营内的水兵无需离开营地即可在此礼拜。

从屋顶向下望去，各种类型的部队单位每隔几分钟就进出封闭的院子，而其他部队则列队站立，等待进一步的操练和命令。

在场记者中无人达成一致意见的一个问题是，这座525英尺乘225英尺建筑的混凝土屋顶的强度。那些认为屋顶仅为普通构造的人，与那些指出屋顶中央放置了用于洗衣目的的混凝土水箱的人激烈反对，后者称承包商除非屋顶得到充分加固，否则不会冒险将此类水箱放置在屋顶上。

枪支充足

向一位日本向导询问后，得到的答复是重型火炮不会从建筑物顶部发射。讨论随之结束。

走到后面，记者和文学观察员群体看到了两门双联装高射炮，安置在小碉堡内。当《大美晚报》代表通过日语翻译向导询问屋顶上一位士官兵营内此类高射武器的数量时，他 cryptic 的回答是：“充足。”

前往兵营的三楼和二楼，一行人穿过看似无尽的水兵宿舍，经过军官房间，进入娱乐室、浴室和水兵食堂。每个作为部队宿舍的大房间旁边，都有较小的步枪、弹药和机枪储藏室。

装甲车停放处

关于存放在兵营内的大型装备，官员称总数为30件，包括口径从三英寸到八英寸的火炮。据说其中包括战壕迫击炮和小型野战炮。

共有九辆装甲车和四辆坦克存放在该建筑的存储空间内，尽管枪支、车辆和坦克所占用的空间仅占此类战争工具可用有顶存储空间的一小部分。

弹药和无线电广播设备的储藏室未向新闻界访客开放视察。日本向导或军方并未试图阻止对建筑物或大院拍照。

兵营的正式落成典礼将推迟至十月某个（续第18页，第3栏。）

（续自第13页，第2栏。）
时间，届时将在东京海军部山本（Yarnamoto，音译）海军上将面前举行日本海军演习。

上海日本海军登陆部队指挥官为杉坂（T. Sugisaka，音译）少将。杉坂少将毕业于日本海军学院，在赴上海任职前曾担任一艘日本战列舰的舰长。

MISCELLANEOUS

China Times and other local newspapers:

A "SHANGHAI SERVANT EMPLOYMENT AGENCIES ASSOCIATION".

Only 50, out of a total of 400, Servant Employment Agencies in Shanghai recently applied to the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang for permission to organize a "Shanghai Servant Employment Agencies Association". The request has been approved by the local Tangpu.
Yesterday a meeting of promoters was held and was presided over by Sun Chiao Po (孙乔甫).
It was decided to divide the Chinese Municipality into five districts, namely Chapei, Eastern District, Western District, French Concession and Nantao.
A preparatory committee of 11 members was also appointed.

THE INSPECTION OF RICSHAS.

The Shanghai Ricsha Owners Association publishes the following advertisement in the Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:-
Two petitions submitted by this Association to the Public Utility Bureau asking for exemption from inspection of ricshas in the Special Districts (Foreign Settlements) have been rejected. The last day of the inspection will be near the end of December. This Association is responsible for conveying this information to the ricsha owners. However, the sending of ricshas to the Bureau for inspection is at the discretion of their owners. This Association therefore will hold a general meeting at 3 p.m. September 16 (Saturday) at its office at San Ping Li (三平里) off Loongneng Road to discuss the question of inspection. All ricsha owners are invited to attend.

Chen Pao publishes the following articles:

THE TERROR OF SHANGHAI.

The anniversary of the tragic September 18 Incident is approaching.
Two years ago (prior to the Wangaochen Tragedy) letters from the Three Eastern Provinces reported that massive new Japanese barracks were being constructed at Changchun. Not long after this, the September 18 Incident took place.
The construction by the Japanese of the huge barracks on an Extra-Settlement Road constitutes a breach of the Washington Pact and the Japanese have stored millions of tons of explosives in Manchuria.

September 15, 1933. Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

The other day the "China Weekly Review,"
edited by Mr. Powell, an American, published an article
strongly criticising the Japanese for their violation
of the Washington Pact. The Japanese forces have
not evacuated Shanghai and have constructed permanent
barracks. It is only natural that there should be
a feeling that the lives and property of foreigners
in this city are in danger. Arising out of this fear,
it is being suggested that the American forces should
not be withdrawn from Shanghai.
The new Japanese barracks are well equipped
and are located at the corner of North Szechuen Road
and Kiengan Road occupying over 100 mou of land.
Anti-aircraft guns and other armaments have been fitted
on the roof of the barracks. A high tower has also
been constructed with telephones and wireless apparatus.

China Times and other local newspapers:

A "SHANGHAI SERVANT EMPLOYMENT AGENCIES ASSOCIATION".

Only 50, out of a total of 400 Servant
Employment Agencies in Shanghai recently applied to the
Shanghai Special District Kuomintang for permission to
organize a "Shanghai Servant Employment Agencies
Association". The request has been approved by the
local Tangpu.
Yesterday a meeting of promotors was held
and was presided over by Sun Chiao Po (孙乔波).
It was decided to divide the Chinese
Municipality into five districts, namely Chapei, Eastern
District, Western District, French Concession and Nantao.
A preparatory committee of 11 members was
also appointed.

THE INSPECTION OF RICSHAS.

The Shanghai Ricsha Owners Association
publishes the following advertisement in the Sin Wan Pao
and other local newspapers:-
Two petitions submitted by this Association
to the Public Utility Bureau asking for exemption from
inspection of ricshas in the Special Districts (Foreign
Settlements) have been rejected. The last day of the
inspection will be near the end of December. This
Association is responsible for conveying this information
to the ricsha owners. However, the sending of ricshas
to the Bureau for inspection is at the discretion of their
owners. This Association therefore will hold a general
meeting at 3 p.m. September 16 (Saturday) at its office
at Sin Ping Li (信平里) off Loongmeng Road to discuss
the question of inspection. All ricsha owners are
invited to attend.

Chen Pao publishes the following articles:

THE TERROR OF SHANGHAI.

The anniversary of the tragic September 18
Incident is approaching.
Two years ago (prior to the Wanpaosan
Tragedy) letters from the Three Eastern Provinces
reported that massive new Japanese barracks were being
constructed at Changchun. Not long after this, the
September 18 Incident took place.
The construction by the Japanese of the
huge barracks on an Extra-Settlement road constitutes
a breach of the Washington Pact and the Japanese have
stored millions of tons of explosives in Shanghai.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 13, 1933. S. B. REGISTER

Chinese Paper's Views On
New Naval Barracks

Japanese "Fortification" Seen As Menace To
Tranquility Of Greater Shanghai And
Infringement Of Sovereign Rights

Commenting editorially on the completion of the new barracks for the Japanese Naval forces, the "Chen Pao" calls attention to the fact that in view of its extreme elaborateness, the structure can only be considered a sort of military fortification and therefore a serious menace to the peace and tranquillity of Greater Shanghai.

Foreign Control

Though the majority of Shanghai's population is Chinese, the journal states, the city has long been under foreign control. With the exception of the French, who occupy a separate part of the city, the British and the Americans are the real masters, while the Japanese share in the administration (of the International Settlement) less prominently. However, the situation has now entirely changed. The Japanese are engaged in a desperate struggle with the British and the Americans for the mastery of Shanghai.

The fact, the journal continues, is clearly borns out by the elaborateness with which the new barracks of the Japanese marine forces (situated near Kiangwan Road and the Shanghai-Woosung Railway) have been constructed. According to military experts, the barracks are able to accommodate 2,600 troops and withstand the heaviest bombardment. Emplacements for heavy guns are constructed on the roof and the windows facing North Szechuan Road can be so transformed as to support machine-guns. The barracks can further house a number of tanks and armoured cars. In view of its location, the structure dominates Kiangwan on the one hand, and controls Chapei on the other.

The new barracks being located in the Extra-Settlement area, the journal points out; it is another flagrant violation by Japan of Sino-Foreign agreements as well as an infringement on China's sovereign rights. The Chinese Government should therefore take appropriate action in conjunction with the various Powers concerned.

Industrial Concentration

Continuing, the paper urges that financial investments be made in the interior of the country "where, of course, the bandits must first be suppressed and peace and order restored." Moreover, it is advisable to have important industries gradually transferred to the hinterland instead of concentrating them in Shanghai. In order to consolidate our national vitality, the paper urges that public buildings should in the future be constructed in an economical and simple manner as possible. Refreshments should be made in the Government Administration...

《字林西报》，1933年9月13日，星期三。特别股登记

中文报纸对新海军兵营的看法

日本“堡垒”被视为对大上海安宁的威胁及对主权的侵犯

《晨报》在社论中评论日本海军新兵营竣工一事时，提请注意这样一个事实：鉴于其极其精细复杂，该建筑只能被视为一种军事堡垒，因此对大上海的和平与安宁构成严重威胁。

外国控制

该报指出，尽管上海人口多数为中国人，但该市长久以来处于外国控制之下。除了占据城市独立部分的法国人外，英国人和美国人是真正的主宰，而日本人在（国际）租界的行政管理中参与度较低。然而，局势现已完全改变。日本人正与英国人和美国人进行殊死斗争，以争夺上海的控制权。

该报继续指出，这一事实由日本海军陆战队新兵营（位于江湾路和沪淞铁路附近）建造的精细程度清楚地证实。据军事专家称，该兵营可容纳2,600名士兵，并能承受最猛烈的轰炸。屋顶建有重型火炮阵地，面向北四川路的窗户可以改造以支撑机枪。兵营还可容纳若干坦克和装甲车。鉴于其位置，该建筑一方面俯瞰江湾，另一方面控制闸北。

该报指出，由于新兵营位于越界筑路区域，这是日本对中外交协定的又一次公然违反，也是对中国主权的侵犯。因此，中国政府应与有关列强采取适当行动。

工业集中

该报接着敦促将金融投资投向内地，“当然，那里必须先剿灭匪患，恢复和平与秩序。”此外，明智的做法是将重要产业逐渐转移至腹地，而不是集中在上海。为了巩固我们的民族活力，该报敦促未来的公共建筑应尽可能经济简朴。政府行政方面应进行整顿……

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 1933

Nipponese
Move Into
New Hongkew
Barracks

Anxiety Is Felt Here
By Foreign Military,
Diplomatic Leaders
Over ‘Fortified Area’

Munitions, Troops Are
Housed In Reinforced
Concrete Structure As
Dedication Is Planned

A condition of anxiety amongst foreign military and diplomatic officials in Shanghai has been openly apparent for the past several weeks.

The feeling of serious uneasiness felt by official representatives of major foreign powers here has been occasioned by the recent completion and proposed dedication of the large Japanese barracks in the Hongkew district on North Szechuen Road, according to the belief of one local foreign consul interviewed by the China Press yesterday.

Although no consular or military officials interviewed yesterday were willing to be quoted there is an apparent feeling that the construction work in progress day and night for the past 10 months that has resulted in the erection of an imposing four-story “barracks” 600 by 250 feet is also far more significance than the mere building of a structure to house troops.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

Full realization of the so-called coup d'etat of the Japanese military was first had by foreign and Chinese officialdom here following the filtering through from Japan of newspaper accounts there telling of Japanese naval maneuvers to be held in the vicinity of Woosung September 15. It has been learned through the same source that elaborate dedication ceremonies of the “barracks” will be held in connection with the maneuvers.

Japanese warships from Hankow, Wuhu and Changsha, as well as others normally stationed up and down the China Coast, have been ordered to the Woosung area by Tokyo naval officers to take part in the maneuvers. It is also planned that several high rank naval officers will also be present to witness the review of troops and warships.

Elaborate Hospital

Apprehensive local foreigners point to the elaborate military hospital, four stories in height and nearly half the size of the former barracks, that has been built in conjunction with the future structure. Together, Japan experts estimate, the cost of construction is in excess of Yen 3,000,000.

Although the structures were started but 10 months ago, following the cessation of the Sino-Japanese hostilities locally, they have been completed in record time. Military officials in Shanghai are said to be of the belief that one of the reasons for the Japanese being able to complete the construction in so short a period of time is that the barracks building is almost a replica of the 3rd Infantry Barracks of the Imperial Army, at Azabu, Tokyo. Following the plans of the sister building in Japan would greatly facilitate speed in construction, it was said.

Both the barracks and hospital have been built of heavily reinforced steel and reinforced concrete that will withstand considerable heavy artillery fire.

The roof of the barracks is reported to be so strongly constructed that five-inch guns could be fired from it without damage to the building itself.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

《字林西报》，1933年9月8日，星期五

日本人
迁入
虹口新
兵营

外国军事、
外交领袖
对“设防区域”
感到焦虑

弹药、部队入驻
钢筋混凝土建筑
落成典礼筹备中

过去几周来，上海外国军事和外交官员中的焦虑状况已公开显现。

据《字林西报》昨日采访的一位当地外国领事认为，驻沪主要列强官方代表所感受到的严重不安，是由位于北四川路虹口区的大型日本兵营近期完工并拟举行落成典礼所致。

虽然昨日接受采访的领事或军事官员均不愿被引述姓名，但显然存在一种感觉，即过去10个月日夜进行的施工工作，建成了一座长600英尺、宽250英尺、气势恢宏的四层“兵营”，其意义远不止于建造一座容纳部队的建筑。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

随着日本报纸关于日军将于9月15日在吴淞附近举行海军演习的报道传入，驻沪外国和中国官界首次充分意识到日本军方的所谓政变。从同一渠道获悉，“兵营”的盛大落成典礼将与演习同时举行。

东京海军军官已命令来自汉口、芜湖和长沙的日本军舰，以及通常驻扎在中国沿海各地的其他军舰，前往吴淞地区参加演习。还计划让几名高级海军军官出席，检阅部队和军舰。

豪华医院

担忧的当地外国人指出，与未来建筑配套建造的是一座四层高、规模接近原兵营一半的豪华军用医院。日本专家估计，两者合计的建设成本超过300万日元。

尽管这些建筑是在当地中日敌对行动停止后仅10个月前开工的，但它们以创纪录的速度完工。据说上海的军事官员认为，日本人之所以能在如此短的时间内完成建设，原因之一是兵营建筑几乎是东京麻布区帝国陆军第三步兵兵营的复制品。据说，沿用日本姊妹楼的设计图纸将大大加快施工速度。

兵营和医院均采用重型钢筋和钢筋混凝土建造，能够承受相当猛烈的重炮火力。

据报道，兵营屋顶结构坚固，即使在其上发射五英寸火炮，也不会对建筑物本身造成损坏。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

(Continued from Page 1, Col. 1.)
been so arranged that the training
and drilling of large numbers of
troops that the structure will house
—variously estimated between 2,000
and 2,500—can be done entirely
within the huge building. There is
even a Shinto Temple in the
rectangular structure that will per-
mit the Japanese faithful to do
their praying within the building.
Room For Tanks
Room has been provided within
for the housing of numerous
armoured cars and tanks. A large
space adjoins this that is being
employed as a storehouse for large
quantities of ammunition that has
been moved in recently.
Electrical power and water is said
to be supplied from a source in the
Chapei district.
So quietly have the Japanese gone
about constructing the buildings
that until recently but few people
were aware of the activity and
practically no one of the significance
of the completed structure as it
stands—a huge fortified reinforced
building capable of being used as
a base for either offensive or de-
fensive warfare.
Whether major foreign powers
will protest the action or move
additional troops into the Shang-
hai area could not be learned yes-
terday. It is claimed by local mili-
tarists (other than Japanese) the
construction of the fortified build-
ings upon Chinese soil is a direct
violation of the Washington Con-
ference Treaty of 1922.
The treaty was adopted in 1922
by the United States, Belgium,
British Empire, France, Italy,
Japan, Portugal and the Nether-
lands. It provided that all foreign
troops on Chinese soil not author-
ed by treaty should be removed.
This was ratified by the Japanese
representatives.
With the closing of the con-
ference Japanese troops at Hankow
and in Shantung Province were
withdrawn. Certain numbers of allied
troops—which included those of
France, Great Britain, Japan and
the United States—were authorized
to be stationed in North China by
the Boxer Protocol. After this date
no further foreign troops were
landed except in cases of extreme
emergency.
Reductions Made
During the 1927 trouble large for-
ces of foreign troops were sent to
Tientsin, Hankow as well as to
Shanghai, but were withdrawn
within a short time from every place
except in Shanghai.
Troops of the countries mention-
ed kept in Shanghai were regarded
by the respective nations as purely
temporary encampments. Evidence
of this, it is pointed out by foreign
military officers, is seen in the fact
that barracks used are either rented
property or hastily constructed
wooden frame structures. All are
to be withdrawn as soon as the
Chinese government is ready to
assume the responsibility of protect-
ing the lives of foreign nationals
and property.
In fact, it is said, there have been
gradual reductions in all forces since
January, 1931, despite the Manchu-
rian trouble. Last year, however,
some 30,000 Japanese troops were
landed on Chinese soil.
Since this time it has been the
plan of America to return the bulk
of her men home; of Great Bri-
tain to send back large numbers
of soldiery to Hongkong, and of
France to dispatch many of the
men wearing her uniform to Indo-
China.
At the present time the total
number of men in foreign uniform in
Shanghai is estimated to be 15,000
(plus or minus).

（续自第1栏第1页。）
布局安排使得该建筑将容纳的大量部队
——估计人数在2,000
至2,500人之间——的训练
和操练可以完全
在这座巨大的建筑内进行。甚至
在这座矩形建筑内还有一座
神道教神社，使
日本信徒可以在建筑内
进行祈祷。
坦克空间
内部提供了空间
用于停放众多
装甲车和坦克。旁边有一大片
空地，正被用作仓库，
储存最近运入的大量
弹药。
据说电力和水源
由闸北地区的一处来源供应。
日本人建造这些建筑物的过程
如此低调，以至于直到最近
很少有人知晓这一活动，
几乎没有人意识到这座已完工建筑
的意义——它是一座巨大的设防加固
建筑，可作为进攻或防御
战争的基地。
至于主要列强是否会抗议
这一行动或向上海地区增派
部队，昨日尚不得而知。
当地军事人士（日本人除外）声称，
在中国领土上建造设防建筑
直接违反了1922年的华盛顿会议条约。
该条约于1922年由美国、比利时、
大英帝国、法国、意大利、
日本、葡萄牙和荷兰通过。条约规定，
所有未经条约授权驻扎在中国领土上的
外国军队均应撤出。
这一点已得到日本代表的批准。
随着会议的结束，驻扎在汉口
和山东省的日本军队
被撤回。根据《辛丑条约》，
一定数量的盟军——包括法国、英国、日本和美国
的军队——获准驻扎在华北。在此日期之后，
除非发生极端紧急情况，否则不再
登陆更多外国军队。
裁减兵力
在1927年的动荡期间，大量
外国军队被派往天津、汉口以及
上海，但除上海外，所有地方的军队
均在短时间内撤出。
留在上海的上述国家军队
被各自国家视为纯粹的
临时营地。外国军事官员指出，
证据在于所使用的兵营要么是
租赁物业，要么是匆忙搭建的
木框架结构。一旦中国政府
准备好承担保护外国侨民
生命和财产的责任，所有军队
都将撤出。
事实上，据说自1931年1月以来，
尽管发生了满洲事变，所有部队
都在逐步减少。然而去年，
约30,000名日本士兵登陆中国领土。
自此以后，美国的计划是将大部分
人员遣返回国；英国计划将大量
士兵送回香港；法国计划将许多
身穿其制服的人员派遣至印度支那。
目前，估计在上海的外国制服人员
总数为15,000人（上下浮动）。

September 14, 1933. Afternoon Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

Chen Pao publishes the following brief comments:

THE NEW JAPANESE MARINE BARRACKS.

The new Japanese barracks at the North Szechuen Road extension are nearing completion. It is being declared that the building can be quickly converted into a well equipped fort in time of war.

A grand review of the local Japanese landing force will take place on September 18. Yesterday morning the Japanese marines held a sham fight. No doubt, all these have come to the special notice of the Chinese residents in Shanghai.

The incidents in the January 28 War are still fresh in our minds. The chief cause why the Japanese forces were so bold as to attack the Chinese in Chapei last year was due to the failure of the International Settlement authorities to check the military activities of the Japanese and permitting the Settlement to be used by the Japanese as a military base. The Chinese forces were thus not in a position to launch counter-attacks. Had the International Settlement not been used as a defense line by the Japanese, the recent hostilities might have had a different ending.

Machine guns and heavy guns in the new Japanese barracks can be directed against Chapei and Kiangwan and the Settlement as well. What is the feeling of the Special District authorities towards the new Japanese barracks?

Sin Wen Pao and other local newspapers:

THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE SEPTEMBER 18 INCIDENT.

The Public Safety Bureau has received the following order from the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioners:-

"I am in receipt of a circular order issued by the Central Propaganda Committee to the effect that on the second anniversary of the September 18 Incident, amusements are to be suspended as a mark of sorrow. At 11 a.m. on that day all members of the Kuomintang Party, the Government officials, soldiers, policemen, public bodies, shops, etc. should observe a five-minute silence, to impress on their hearts to avenge the national humiliation and to commemorate the North-Eastern martyrs."

General Wan Hung An, Commissioner of the Public Safety Bureau, has directed his subordinates to take note and act accordingly.

《申报》刊登如下简短评论：

日本海军陆战队新营房。

位于北四川路延伸段的日本新营房即将竣工。据称，该建筑在战时可迅速改建为装备精良的堡垒。

驻沪日本登陆部队将于9月18日举行盛大阅兵。昨晨，日本海军陆战队举行了演习。毫无疑问，所有这些已引起上海中国居民的特别注意。

“一·二八”战事的种种事件仍历历在目。去年日军之所以如此大胆地进攻闸北的中国军队，主要原因在于国际租界当局未能遏制日军的军事活动，并允许租界被日军用作军事基地。中国军队因此无法发动反击。如果日军未将国际租界用作防线，最近的敌对行动可能会有不同的结局。

新日本营房内的机枪和重炮可以指向闸北、江湾以及租界本身。特区当局对新日本营房持何种态度？

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

“九一八”事变周年纪念。

公安局收到淞沪警备司令部的如下命令：——

“兹接中央宣传委员会通令，值此‘九一八’事变两周年之际，为示哀悼，暂停娱乐活动。是日上午11时，所有国民党党员、政府官员、军人、警察、公共团体、商店等，应默哀五分钟，以铭记国耻、誓图雪恨，并纪念东北殉难烈士。”

公安局长万鸿恩将军已指示下属知悉并遵照执行。

Date 12. 9. 33.

September 12, 1933. Afternoon Translated.

MISCELLANEOUS

Chen Pao (Editorial):

THE TERROR OF SHANGHAI.

The ceremony commemorating the re-construction of the Shanghai North Station, which was demolished by enemy gunfire during the January 28 War, took place the other day.

People who have never been in Shanghai but have heard of the prosperity of this city are anxious to pay a visit. Upon their arrival here, they see towering mansions, thriving industrial and commercial enterprises and every modernism. They regard Shanghai as a peaceful modern village, but they are not aware of the fact that apart from the economic hardships of the community there are other dangers which are quite sufficient to ruin Shanghai as a whole.

Ninety per cent of the residents of Shanghai are Chinese, yet Shanghai does not belong to the Chinese people. Generally speaking, this city belongs to the British and American people with the Japanese enjoying a share.

The Japanese who occupy a position of lesser importance in Shanghai have commenced a vigorous struggle to grasp Shanghai. Information from local Japanese merchants reveals that the ambitious Japanese have copies of a picture in their homes to serve as a warning to themselves. The picture depicts a hawk and a devil about to seize a sun. The devil represents America, while the hawk is Britain. It means that Japan will be ruined if she does not fight Britain and America for her existence and to secure control of affairs in East Asia. The first step the Japanese will take in this respect is to remove the influence of Britain and America in Shanghai and then to drive away the British and Americans from East Asia, so that China will come under the protection of Japan.

The new Japanese barracks on Kiangwan Road reveals Japan's intentions in Shanghai. Military experts declare that these new barracks are in a position to withstand heavy gunfire, big guns can be fired from the top of the barracks and machine guns can be fixed to the windows of the building facing North Szechuen Road in order to threaten the Settlement. As the site of the barracks is close to the Woosung-Shanghai railway, it is quite easy for the Japanese to menace Chapei and Kiangwan.

The construction by the Japanese of this fort on an Extra-Settlement road constitutes a violation of China's territorial rights and an infringement of the treaties. The Chinese Government should unite with the foreign authorities concerned to devise ways and means to deal with the matter.

To whom will Shanghai belong in future? Only the efforts of the Chinese people can influence the reply to this question.

（批：D. 4407）

1933年9月12日。下午译件。

杂项

《申报》（社论）：

上海之恐怖。

日前举行了纪念上海北站重建的仪式，该站在“一·二八”战事中被敌军炮火摧毁。

未曾到过上海但听闻此城繁荣的人，都渴望前来一游。当他们抵达此处，看到高耸的宅邸、兴盛的工商业以及各类现代设施。他们将上海视为一个和平的现代村落，却未意识到这样一个事实：除了社区的经济困难外，还有其他危险足以彻底毁掉上海。

上海居民百分之九十是中国人，但上海并不属于中国人民。一般而言，这座城市属于英美人士，日本人也占有一席之地。

在上海地位较次要的日本人已开始为夺取上海而进行激烈斗争。来自当地日本商人的消息显示，野心勃勃的日本人在家中备有一幅图画以自警。画中描绘一只鹰和一个魔鬼正欲攫取太阳。魔鬼代表美国，鹰代表英国。这意味着，如果日本不为生存而战并确立对东亚事务的控制权，日本将会灭亡。日本在此方面的第一步将是消除英美在上海的影响，然后将英美逐出东亚，从而使中国处于日本的保护之下。

位于江湾路的新日本营房揭示了日本在上海的意图。军事专家宣称，这些新营房能够承受猛烈炮火，营房顶部可发射大炮，面向北四川路的窗户可安装机枪，以威胁租界。由于营房地址靠近淞沪铁路，日军很容易威胁闸北和江湾。

日本在越界筑路区域建造这座堡垒，构成了对中国领土主权的侵犯和对条约的违背。中国政府应与有关外国当局联合，制定办法处理此事。

上海未来将属于谁？只有中国人民的努力才能影响这一问题的答案。

（批注：D. 4407）

MISCELLANEOUS

China Evening News:

THE JAPANESE FORCES IN SHANGHAI.

Since the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai, the Japanese forces here have been provided with extensive military equipment. A Third Japanese Fleet has recently been organised and will be stationed in Shanghai. The strength of the Japanese Landing Force has been increased from 400 to some 2,500 men and has been equipped with heavy guns, light guns, tanks and other weapons and is able to deal with a Division of troops. (Rear-Admiral Sugisaka, Commander of the Japanese Landing Force, the other day proudly boasted that the marines were in a position to fight an enemy of over ten thousand men.) The number of the Japanese Police has been increased from ten to more than 200 men and the Police Department has been re-organised. There is a Japanese Gendarme Corps. The expansion of the association of Japanese ex-service men and the formation of Japanese youth armies indicate the Japanese preparations for a war in Shanghai.

The massive Japanese barracks at the corner of North Szechuen Road and Kiangwan Road has attracted the most attention. The Japanese Naval Office commenced the construction of the new barracks in Spring 1932 at the huge cost of Yen 20,000,000. The barracks are nearing completion and a section of Japanese bluejackets removed into the new barracks on September 5.

The barracks consist of a 3-story building containing 1,300 rooms. The top of the building can accommodate 5,000 to 6,000 men. On the western side of the roof stands a tower in the neighbourhood of which are numerous signal rooms and secret rooms.

According to a certain Japanese, the plan of the barracks is being kept very secret. The engineers, carpenters, etc. were detailed to Shanghai from the Sasebo Naval Base. No admittance was allowed to anybody during the period of construction. There are also extensive underground rooms which can not only accommodate the entire body of Japanese marines in Shanghai but can give shelter to all Japanese residents in this city in case of emergency. A secret long-wave radio station is installed on the roof for direct communication with radio stations in Tokyo, Dairen, Hankow, etc. Heavy gun emplacements have been constructed around the barracks.

A certain foreign military observer states that the Japanese barracks are not of the ordinary kind and had been constructed for permanent use.

Upon the completion of the new barracks, the Japanese marines now stationed in Yangtsepoo district will remove into the barracks.

Rear-Admiral Sugisaka will hold a grand ceremony on September 13 to celebrate the completion of the barracks with a review of Japanese bluejackets in the Hongkew Park.

（左侧手写批注：DHW07 S）

杂项

《China Evening News》：

驻沪日军。

自上海中日敌对行动以来，驻沪日军已配备大量军事装备。日本第三舰队最近已组建，并将驻扎于上海。日本登陆部队的人数已从400人增加至约2,500人，并配备了重炮、轻炮、坦克和其他武器，有能力应对一个师的兵力。（日本登陆部队指挥官杉坂少将日前自豪地吹嘘，海军陆战队有能力对抗一万多名敌人。）日本警察人数已从十人增加至二百多人，警察部门已重组。设有一支日本宪兵队。日本退伍军人协会的扩张和日本青年军的组建，表明日本正在为上海战争做准备。

位于北四川路与江湾路转角处的庞大日本营房最受关注。日本海军办事处于1932年春季开始建造新营房，耗资巨大，达2,000万日元。营房即将竣工，一部分日本水兵已于9月5日迁入新营房。

营房由一栋三层建筑组成，包含1,300个房间。建筑顶部可容纳5,000至6,000人。屋顶西侧矗立着一座塔楼，附近有许多信号室和密室。

据某位日本人称，营房的平面图保密极严。工程师、木匠等人员是从佐世保海军基地调派至上海的。施工期间禁止任何人进入。还有广泛的地下室，不仅可以容纳驻沪全体日本海军陆战队队员，而且在紧急情况下可以为该市所有日本居民提供庇护。屋顶安装有一个秘密长波电台，用于与东京、大连、汉口等地的电台直接通信。营房周围已修建重炮阵地。

一位外国军事观察家指出，日本营房并非普通类型，而是为永久使用而建造的。

新营房竣工后，目前驻扎在杨树浦地区的日本海军陆战队将迁入该营房。

杉坂少将将于9月13日举行盛大仪式，庆祝营房竣工，并在虹口公园检阅日本水兵。

（左侧手写批注：DHW07 S）

Dear Dicker,

With reference to your inquiry by telephone, it has been learned that the buildings to be used as barracks for the Japanese Naval Landing Party are being constructed on the North and South sides of N. Szechuen Road Extension near the point where this thoroughfare joins Kiangwan Road. The barracks are being constructed with reinforced concrete and steel and will be four storeys in height. The building on the North of N. Szechuen Road Extension will be used by non-commissioned officers and men and the one on the South by commissioned officers. The buildings will provide accommodation for 2,008 officers and men and are expected to be ready for occupation about July 1935.

The site on the North side of N. Szechuen Road Extension covers about 11 mow. It extends from Kiangwan Road on the East to Wengle Road on the West and Northward from North Szechuen Road for a distance of about 400 feet. The building on this site will be erected in the form of a square and will have a drill ground in the centre. The ground floor will be used for storing provisions, equipments and military mechanical contrivances.

The site on the South side of North Szechuen Road covers about 3 kow and is situated immediately east of the Swimming Bath.
